units.text: INT. RAILWAY WAITING ROOM - NIGHT (1884)
A cold hall of benches and a cast-iron stove.
Gaslight hisses.
Snow has stopped the last train.
MRS. HARRIET COLLINGWOOD, sixties, in black bombazine, knits by the stove.
A MAN in a worn greatcoat sits on the far bench, hat low, a carpetbag between his boots.
Good evening, ma'am.
units.name: MAN

units.text: It is not, sir. It is snowing.
units.name: HARRIET

units.text: So it is.
units.name: MAN

units.text: She knits.
The needles click.
He rubs his hands.
Are you waiting for the Dover connection?
units.name: MAN

units.text: I am waiting for my nephew. He is meant to meet me.
units.name: HARRIET

units.text: In this?
units.name: MAN

units.text: He is a very unreliable young man.
units.name: HARRIET

units.text: The man laughs, a short warm sound.
And you, sir? You have the look of a person who has been waiting longer than a night.
units.name: HARRIET

units.text: Twenty years, ma'am. My name is Elias Fairchild.
units.name: MAN

units.text: Harriet's needles stop.
She looks up for the first time.
Fairchild. You are Charles's brother.
units.name: HARRIET

units.text: I am.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: He spoke of you with great bitterness.
units.name: HARRIET

units.text: He had cause.
units.name: ELIAS

units.text: She resumes knitting.
After a moment she pats the bench beside her.
Elias crosses the hall and sits.
